title: Arjun Badola and Dikshit Hegde win QIF India 2026
headline: India 2026
summary: Arjun Badola and Dikshit Hegde have won the Qualcomm Innovation Fellowship India 2026 for their proposal on transparent 3D Gaussian splatting, advised by Prof. Shanmuganathan Raman.
proposal: Frequency-Adaptive Prior Supervision for Transparent 3D Gaussian Splatting
proposalLines:
Frequency-Adaptive Prior Supervision
for Transparent 3D Gaussian Splatting
caption: Congratulations to Arjun Badola and Dikshit Hegde on winning the Qualcomm Innovation Fellowship India 2026. Their proposal, ‘Frequency-Adaptive Prior Supervision for Transparent 3D Gaussian Splatting’, is advised by Prof. Shanmuganathan Raman at IIT Gandhinagar.
illustrationDescription: The torus is a doughnut-shaped surface. The Gaussian version uses overlapping elliptical contours, the low-poly version uses triangular faces, and the simple version uses a wireframe. These are conceptual illustrations, not results from the awarded project.

title: Ayush Shrivastava and Rohit Narayanan selected for TCS PhD fellowships
headline: PhD fellowships
summary: Ayush Shrivastava and Rohit Narayanan have been selected for the TCS Research Scholar Program, Cycle 20, with fellowships effective 1 July 2026.
caption: Congratulations to Ayush Shrivastava and Rohit Narayanan on their selection for the TCS Research Scholar Program, Cycle 20. Ayush is advised by Prof. Nipun Batra and Prof. Mayank Goel; Rohit is advised by Prof. Balagopal Komarath. The fellowships are effective 1 July 2026.

people.name: Ayush Shrivastava
people.advisers: Prof. Nipun Batra and Prof. Mayank Goel
people.adviserLines:
Prof. Nipun Batra
and Prof. Mayank Goel

illustrationDescription: Ayush: a synthetic thermal patch and waveform evoke thermal health sensing. Rohit: a small monotone arithmetic formula evokes his work on bounded-depth formula complexity. These are original topic illustrations, not research measurements, paper figures or claims about the funded fellowship proposals.

title: Three CSE PhD students receive IndiaAI PhD Fellowships
headline: PhD fellowships
caption: Congratulations to Naren Kumar, Manvendra Singh and Dikshit Hegde on receiving IndiaAI PhD Fellowships. Their advisers are Prof. Mayank Singh, Prof. Anirban Dasgupta and Prof. Shanmuganathan Raman, respectively.
illustrationDescription: An original layered learning-network schematic evokes AI research. It does not depict any of the recipients’ fellowship proposals or results.
photoNote: The official directory provides placeholder images for Naren and Manvendra. A complete name-led layout gives equal space to all three recipients.

title: MCP-Diag recognized at COMSNETS 2026 Graduate Forum
headline: MCP-Diag
caption: Congratulations to Devansh Lodha, Mohit Panchal and Prof. Sameer G. Kulkarni. Their paper, “MCP-Diag: A Deterministic, Protocol-Driven Architecture for AI-Native Network Diagnostics”, received the Graduate Forum Best Paper Runner-up award at COMSNETS 2026.
illustrationDescription: An original network-to-diagnostics diagram introduces the paper’s subject. The observe/check/explain sequence is conceptual, not the paper’s exact architecture.
detailLines:
A Deterministic, Protocol-Driven Architecture
for AI-Native Network Diagnostics
peopleLines:
Devansh Lodha · Mohit Panchal
Prof. Sameer G. Kulkarni

title: Himanshu Beniwal receives Microsoft Research India PhD Award and Fulbright-Nehru Fellowship
headline: Research honours
caption: Congratulations to Himanshu Beniwal on receiving the Microsoft Research India PhD Award 2025 and the Fulbright-Nehru Doctoral Research Fellowship 2025-26. He carried out his doctoral research with Prof. Mayank Singh at IIT Gandhinagar.
illustrationDescription: Two language streams enter a shared model, an original conceptual illustration of multilingual NLP. It is not a specific model architecture or an experimental result.

title: Gayatri Priyadarsini Kancherla receives Google PhD Fellowship
headline: Class of 2025
caption: Congratulations to Gayatri Priyadarsini Kancherla on receiving a 2025 Google PhD Fellowship in Privacy, Safety, and Security.
illustrationDescription: A browser window shows scripts with allowed and blocked access to persistent storage. Inspired by Gayatri’s paper on least-privilege browser-storage access; this is an original schematic, not an assertion that this specific paper received the fellowship.

title: Dharaben R. Thakkar receives ACM India Doctoral Dissertation Award
headline: Dissertation Award
caption: Congratulations to Dr. Dharaben R. Thakkar on receiving the ACM India Doctoral Dissertation Award 2025 for “On Computing Optimal Representations of Finite Groups”. Her doctoral adviser was Prof. Bireswar Das at IIT Gandhinagar.
illustrationDescription: The cyclic group of order five is drawn with addition of one modulo five. It is an introductory finite-group example, not a result or construction from the dissertation.
detailLines:
On Computing Optimal Representations
of Finite Groups

title: Anirban Dasgupta receives STOC 2024 Test of Time Award
award: ACM Symposium on Theory of Computing
headline: Test of Time Award
caption: Prof. Anirban Dasgupta, Ravi Kumar and Tamás Sarlós received the STOC 2024 10-year Test of Time Award for “A Sparse Johnson-Lindenstrauss Transform”, published in 2010. Congratulations to the authors.
illustrationDescription: A sparse matrix maps a longer coordinate vector to a shorter one, illustrating the dimension-reduction idea in the awarded paper. The displayed toy matrix illustrates shape and sparsity only; it is not the paper’s construction and does not claim a distance-preservation guarantee.
creditLines: Anirban Dasgupta · Ravi Kumar · Tamás Sarlós
